content_summary: Rolling a deploy is a coin flip for us now: half the workers lose the broker mid-drain and the tasks that were running come back as connection errors.
Our distro dropped the exceptiongroup package and now the worker won't even boot on Python 3.12. We're pinning an old release until this is sorted.
Our dashboard shows revoked jobs as PENDING until something picks them up. For ETA jobs that's basically forever and support keeps asking about it.
Adding -B to our gevent worker used to print a helpful 'run beat standalone' message. Now it's just an AttributeError about a str having no __module__.
Retries on our quorum queues just evaporate. RabbitMQ logs a dead-letter cycle and the task never comes back. Took us two days to even notice.
Ctrl-C on an eventlet worker throws 'do not call blocking functions from the mainloop' instead of shutting down. Have to kill -9 every time.
Every Monday morning the first few jobs fail with 'MySQL server has gone away'. Everyone I know using the database backend just adds pool_pre_ping by hand.
Embedded beat comes back from a process restart pointing at the wrong app. The arguments look scrambled when you print the rebuilt object.
Six chords in a chain produced a 1.4 GB message and took the broker down with it. Five was already 120 MB. We had to hand-roll the workflow instead.
Chains sometimes stop halfway with nothing in the logs. It seems to happen on the runs where a message got redelivered.
`celery status` printing a full traceback when the broker is down is a rough first experience. New folks on the team think they broke something.
apply_async(ignore_result=False) does nothing for a task declared with ignore_result=True. We ended up defining the same task twice.
After a Redis failover the workers look healthy in ps but consume nothing. Only a restart brings them back.
Happy to see the CLI errors getting attention. Would love `inspect` and `control` to be as readable as the rest.
